instructions: Shuck the corn and pull off the silk. Stand each ear upright on a cutting board and slice the kernels off in strips, cutting away from your hand.
Put the kernels in a large pot with the 1 cup broth, the 4 cups water and 1 tsp salt. Bring to a boil.
Turn the heat to medium and cook, stirring now and then, until about two thirds of the liquid is gone. That should be about 20 minutes. Drain off what's left.
Stir the 2 tbsp butter into the hot corn until it melts.
Spoon the corn into 4 cups. Top each with a spoonful of the 3 tbsp mayonnaise, some of the 1/4 cup cotija and a dusting of the 1/2 tsp chili powder.
Squeeze the lime over the cups. Serve warm with the hot sauce on the side for anyone who wants it.
method_notes: Mamá Maggie's Kitchen leads: kernels simmered in broth and water until most of the liquid cooks off, then layered in cups with mayo, cotija, chili powder, butter, lime and hot sauce. Her page lists a 5 hour cook time that looks like a typo, and her toppings are very light, so mayo and cotija are set a little higher, in line with My Everyday Table's skillet version (frozen corn, mayo and crema, cotija, lime, Tajin). Vegetable broth keeps it vegetarian; the heat is left to the table.
